questions.text:
Which of the following is/are the eigenvector(s) for the matrix given below?
[latex] \begin{pmatrix} -9 &-6 &-2 &-4 \\ -8& -6 & -3 & -1 \\ 20 & 15 & 8 & 5 \\ 32& 21& 7&12 \end{pmatrix}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Multiply the matrix by each vector and check if the result is a multiple of it:
- [latex](-1,1,0,1)\rightarrow(-1,1,0,1)[/latex] = 1[latex]\cdot[/latex]v True
- [latex](1,0,-1,0)\rightarrow(-7,-5,12,25)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not a multiple False
- [latex](-1,0,2,2)\rightarrow(-3,0,6,6)[/latex] = 3[latex]\cdot[/latex]v True
- [latex](0,1,-3,0)\rightarrow(0,3,-9,0)[/latex] = 3[latex]\cdot[/latex]v True

Answer: Options 1, 3 and 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Using Doolittle LU (unit diagonal in L):
- Row 1 of U = [1, 1, [latex]-[/latex]2]; [latex]L_{21}=1,\ L_{31}=2[/latex]
- [latex]U_{22}=3-1=2,\ U_{23}=-1-(-2)=1[/latex]
- [latex]L_{32}=\frac{1-2\cdot1}{2}=-\frac12[/latex]
- [latex]U_{33}=-5-2(-2)-(-\frac12)(1)=-\frac12[/latex]

Solving the system: eq2 [latex]-[/latex] eq1 gives [latex]2x_2+x_3=3[/latex]; eq3 [latex]-[/latex] 2[latex]\cdot[/latex]eq1 gives [latex]x_2+x_3=1[/latex]. So [latex]x_2=2,\ x_3=-1,\ x_1=4-2-2=0[/latex].

Answer: [latex]L_{32}=-\frac12,\ U_{33}=-\frac12,\ x_1=0[/latex]

questions.text:
The value of the following limit is _____
[latex] \lim_{x \to 0+} \frac{ \sqrt{x}}{1-e^{2 \sqrt{x}}}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Let [latex]t=\sqrt x\to0^+[/latex]: the limit is [latex]\lim_{t\to0}\frac{t}{1-e^{2t}}[/latex] (form 0/0).

Since [latex]e^{2t}\approx1+2t[/latex]: [latex]\frac{t}{1-e^{2t}}\approx\frac{t}{-2t}=-\frac12[/latex] (same by L'Hospital: [latex]\frac{1}{-2e^{2t}}\to-\frac12[/latex]).

Answer: -0.5

questions.text:
Consider the following two statements with respect to the matrices [latex]A_{m \times n},B_{n \times m},C_{n \times n} \text{ and }D_{n \times n},[/latex]

Statement 1: [latex]tr(AB) = tr(BA)[/latex]
Statement 2: [latex]tr(CD) = tr(DC)[/latex]

where[latex]tr()[/latex] represents the trace of a matrix. Which one of the following holds?
questions.solution:
[latex]tr(AB)=\sum_i\sum_k a_{ik}b_{ki}=\sum_k\sum_i b_{ki}a_{ik}=tr(BA)[/latex]. This holds for any [latex]A_{m\times n}[/latex], [latex]B_{n\times m}[/latex] (AB is [latex]m\times m[/latex], BA is [latex]n\times n[/latex]).

Statement 2 is the special case of square matrices, so it is also true.

Answer: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct

Statement 1 is wrong and Statement 2 is correct.
Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct.

questions.text:
For two n-dimensional real vectors [latex]P[/latex] and [latex]Q[/latex], the operation [latex]s(P,Q)[/latex] is defined as follows:

[latex]s(P,Q) = \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n (P[i] \cdot Q[i])[/latex]

Let [latex]\mathcal{L}[/latex] be a set of 10-dimensional non-zero real vectors such that for every pair of distinct vectors [latex]P,Q \in \mathcal{L}, s(P,Q)=0[/latex]. What is the maximum cardinality possible for the set [latex]\mathcal{L}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
s(P, Q) is the dot product, so the set contains mutually orthogonal non-zero vectors. Such vectors are linearly independent, and [latex]\mathbb{R}^{10}[/latex] has at most 10 independent vectors (e.g. the 10 unit vectors).

Answer: 10
